deficiencies.description: The lecturer made a general remark that comparing 'any two things' will reveal differences, whereas the rewrite changes and narrows this to 'any comparison between two species'.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: if you compare any two things, you're going to find differences
deficiencies.rewritePassage: any comparison between two species will reveal differences

deficiencies.description: The lecturer stated that the fivefold higher rate in reptiles was 'the only thing that was quite interesting to note here', but the rewrite characterizes it as '[t]he one notable difference', asserting that it is the sole notable difference between the groups.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: The only thing that was quite interesting to note here is that the rate of malignant tumors is about fivefold higher in reptiles compared to mammals.
deficiencies.rewritePassage: The one notable difference is that the rate of malignant tumours is about fivefold higher in reptiles than in mammals

considerations.sourcePassage: they very much get similar tumors to us
considerations.reason: Rendering 'to us' as 'those of humans' adapts the spoken lecture style into textbook prose with the exact same meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: mammary tumors seem to be very, very prevalent
considerations.reason: Dropping the second 'very' removes a spoken repetition/emphasis without altering the meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: And this is my cat, who also ended up with a feline injection site sarcoma.
considerations.reason: Shifting from first-person 'my cat' to 'The lecturer's own cat' is an allowed stylistic change for textbook prose.

considerations.sourcePassage: You'll be happy to hear he's doing fine now after his surgery.
considerations.reason: Omitting 'You'll be happy to hear' drops a direct remark to the audience while retaining the factual claim that the cat is doing fine after surgery.
Writing 'hematopoietic tissues' completes the elliptical spoken phrasing to match 'digestive tissues' in parallel structure.
